Only generalize when the evaluation summary indicates a systemic issue, but otherwise don't overgeneralize bullet points. Generally respect the BFCL evaluation but think about what you would want to tell the model in order for it to improve in the many cases it may face in the future.keep the playbook unchanged on successes unless an existing entry now conflicts with verified behaviour. Functional parity with the checker matters more than superficial differences . Output JSON.

Tool groups: message_api, vehicle_control_api

Existing playbook:
ACE Playbook Insights
Use these distilled reminders to plan tool usage. Keep tool calls faithful to the functions provided in the BFCL benchmark.

message_api
- delta1: When user provides their own ID, send confirmation message back to them immediately.
- delta2: User ID disclosure triggers send_message to that user immediately, using provided IDs directly without validation
- delta3: Continue message operations across all conversation turns regardless of user input brevity.
- delta4: Execute message_login and send_message directly when user IDs are explicitly provided, without validation or discovery calls
- delta5: Maintain consistent internal state tracking across all API instances throughout multi-turn conversations
- delta6: Use provided user IDs directly without attempting to discover or validate them through additional API calls
- delta7: Avoid message_get_login_status calls when login state can be inferred from context or user requirements

vehicle_control_api
- delta1: Always press brake pedal before attempting engine start - safety requirement
- delta10: Avoid redundant status checks - single call per inquiry prevents state drift in multi-turn scenarios
- delta11: Avoid redundant displayCarStatus calls that don't advance vehicle state in multi-turn scenarios
- delta12: Use actual calculated distance for estimate_drive_feasibility_by_mileage calls - never use zero or placeholder values
- delta13: Call set_navigation when directing to any destination - includes tire shops when pressures are below threshold
- delta14: Attempt distance estimation and feasibility checks with available location data - don't block all operations due to partial information
- delta15: Use get_zipcode_based_on_city for location discovery when destination city is provided but details are incomplete
- delta16: Execute fillFuelTank with calculated amount when full tank is requested - never block on fuel level inquiries
- delta17: Use get_zipcode_based_on_city immediately when destination city is known - don't block operations waiting for user input
- delta18: Execute fillFuelTank immediately when fuel is insufficient - don't wait for user confirmation or manual intervention
- delta19: Release brake pedal after successful engine start - complete the full brake→start→release sequence
- delta2: Only recommend tire shops when pressure is actually below specified threshold
- delta20: Execute pending vehicle operations on empty user turns - maintain state continuity across all conversation turns
- delta21: Avoid function commentary when user input is empty - prioritize executing required vehicle control actions
- delta3: Execute fillFuelTank with precise calculation - iterative approaches are acceptable if they achieve correct final state
- delta4: Complete vehicle start sequence with brake pedal first, then single engine start, then release brake - never skip brake application or release
- delta5: Avoid redundant status checks that don't advance vehicle state - displayCarStatus calls should serve operational purposes
- delta6: Execute engine start sequence only once after proper brake pedal application - avoid multiple redundant start attempts
- delta7: Call estimate_drive_feasibility_by_mileage once per scenario - iterative checks acceptable for state discovery
- delta8: Include set_navigation when destination is specified in trip planning context
- delta9: Lock all doors before attempting engine start - safety requirement to prevent unauthorized access
